Strong cold front arrives to North Georgia!

By
Tyler Penland
-
November 12, 2026| Updated: 26 days ago
Facebook
Twitter
Email
Print
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:29
    Instaread

    The first truly strong cold front of the year is expected to arrive in North Georgia Wednesday night.

    Showers are likely overnight in the midnight-3 a.m. range just ahead of or along the initial front. Rainfall could be briefly heavy, but totals will be very light with the quick-moving storms and the highest totals will come the further north/west you live.

    Behind the front winds will turn gusty with gusts of 25-30 m.p.h. expected for most Thursday, and up to 35 m.p.h. across the higher elevations. Additional moisture will come through in waves on Friday as an upper level trough moves through, and flurries or brief light snow showers are possible across most of the mountain counties northwest of roughly a Clayton to Helen to Amicalola line. No accumulation is likely (or even possible, ground is too warm).

    Afternoon highs on Friday will be very chilly, with the mountains reaching only the mid-40s and the rest of the region around 50º.

    Refurbed
    refurbed.de
    >

    A widespread frost/freeze is likely both Friday and Saturday nights. The mountains will dip well into the 20s both nights with the foothills around or just below freezing.

    Highs for Saturday will likely stick in the upper-40s again for the mountains and low/mid-50s for the foothills, with temps a few degrees warmer on Sunday.

    Refurbed
    refurbed.de
    >

    Enjoy the first cold blast!
